notes: Live Atlassian MCP fetch is non-deterministic in eval subagents, so each prompt supplies the ticket as a file (treated as already-fetched) plus a small fixture codebase to verify claims against. Evals 1-3 leave the approval gate intact, so autonomous runs stop at phase 5 (present-for-approval) without editing — phases 2-4 (intent, claim verification, plan reconciliation) are the differentiated value being graded there. Eval 4 is the exception: it pre-grants approval in the prompt so the run proceeds into phase 6 (implement) and works against a copy of the fixture, to exercise and grade the red/green TDD discipline that the other evals never reach.

evals.name: flawed-proposed-solution
evals.prompt: You're picking up JIRA ticket CHK-1190. The Atlassian fetch has already been done — the full ticket content is in /Users/jfatras/Projects/Claude/jira-implement-workspace/fixtures/eval-2-flawed-solution/ticket.md (treat it as the fetched ticket; getJiraIssue is unavailable, so read the file). The working codebase is the directory /Users/jfatras/Projects/Claude/jira-implement-workspace/fixtures/eval-2-flawed-solution/codebase/ (orders.js as src/orders.js, schema.sql as the orders migration). Pick up and action this ticket.
evals.expected_output: Verifies the ticket's claims as true (no uniqueness constraint beyond PK in schema.sql; submitOrder inserts unconditionally in orders.js) with evidence. Designs its own plan before adopting the ticket's in-memory Set approach. Catches that an in-memory Set is unsafe given the service runs as 4 PM2 cluster workers (the Set isn't shared across processes and is lost on restart), and instead recommends a durable mechanism (DB unique constraint / idempotency key). Reconciliation keeps the author's dedup intent/signature idea but rejects in-memory storage, naming per-dimension winners. Stops at the approval gate before editing.

assertions.text: Verifies the 'no uniqueness constraint' and 'unconditional insert' claims as true/confirmed with file:line evidence
Designs an independent plan before adopting or endorsing the ticket's proposed in-memory Set
Identifies that the in-memory Set is unsafe under multi-process/cluster execution (4 PM2 workers) and/or lost on restart
Recommends a durable dedup mechanism (DB unique constraint or idempotency key) instead of the in-memory Set
Reconciliation names per-dimension winners and mines the proposed solution for its useful parts (dedup goal / signature concept) rather than discarding or rubber-stamping it
Stops at an approval gate before editing any file

evals.name: tdd-happy-path
evals.prompt: You're picking up JIRA ticket STR-310. The Atlassian fetch has already been done — the full ticket content is in /Users/jfatras/Projects/Claude/jira-implement-workspace/fixtures/eval-4-tdd/ticket.md (treat it as the fetched ticket; getJiraIssue is unavailable in this environment, so read the file instead). The working codebase is the directory /Users/jfatras/Projects/Claude/jira-implement-workspace/fixtures/eval-4-tdd/codebase/ (pluralize.js is src/pluralize.js, pluralize.test.js is its test file). It is a zero-dependency Node 24 project; run the tests with `node --test pluralize.test.js` (or `npm test`) from inside the codebase directory. IMPORTANT: do not edit the original fixture — copy the entire codebase/ directory into your designated output directory and make every change there, leaving the original pristine. You have approval to proceed all the way through implementation without pausing at the approval gate: treat the plan as pre-approved, briefly state it, then implement it. Pick up and action this ticket.
evals.expected_output: Verifies the ticket's claim that pluralize has no consonant+y handling as TRUE with file:line evidence from pluralize.js (the regex only covers sibilants; no -y branch). Premise is sound, so it proceeds. In the implement phase it works test-first: writes a NEW failing test for the consonant+y cases (category→categories, city→cities) and runs it to observe RED before touching pluralize.js, then adds the minimal consonant+y → -ies rule (preserving vowel+y like day→days and all existing behavior), then re-runs the suite to observe GREEN with the pre-existing tests still passing. Reports the actual test output honestly. Final code passes node --test.

assertions.text: Verifies the 'no consonant+y handling' claim as confirmed/true with file:line evidence from pluralize.js (sibilant-only regex, no -y branch)
Treats the premise as sound and proceeds to implement (does not manufacture a false positive or stall)
Writes a NEW failing test for the consonant+y cases (category→categories and/or city→cities) BEFORE editing pluralize.js
Runs the test and observes it FAIL (RED) before writing the implementation, rather than implementing first
Implements the minimal consonant+y → -ies rule, preserving vowel+y (day→days, boy→boys) and all existing cases
Re-runs the suite and observes it PASS (GREEN) with the pre-existing tests still passing
Reports actual test-run output honestly (quotes the real red and green runs) rather than asserting an unobserved green
